Messages.Author: Silmegil
Messages.Body:
419 Operation
Type: Action
Requires: Osebo
+1 stealth action.
Put this card in play. During your untap phase, you may move 1 pool from your prey's pool to this card or move the pool on this card to your pool. Your prey can burn the Edge to move the counters on this card to his or her pool and burn this card.

I need little help with this card and its wording. I am little confused, since english is not my native language. Expecially the part:" move the pool on this card to your pool." So my question is this: I have 2+ pool counters on this card. Can I move all of those counters to my pool at once or only one of them?

I was trying to find this ruling somwhere online, but problem is probably more my understanding of english than card wording. Thank you for help.

czechvtes.blogspot.com/

Messages.Author: Boris The Blade
Messages.Body:
Yes, you move all of it. Observe the difference between the wordings of the two effects:

-During your untap phase, you may move 1 pool from your prey's pool to this card
-or move the pool on this card to your pool.

If the second effect was meant to be 1 pool only, it would be written 1 pool.

Messages.Author: Kiddo
Messages.Body:
So basically, in order to remove the card (and retrieve all the pool lost currently on the Operation), the prey just has to successfully bleed (and burn the edge), right?

So this is a card that forces your prey to bleed, rather than, for example, wall-up and defend his Smiling Jack?

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
> Non-existant user wrote:
> Yes, you move all of it.
>
Correct.

> Pool: A token representing a Methuselah's status. Also, a collection of such tokens.
>
Using "pool" for "all the pool counters" (or blood) happens from time to time, but a good rule is to assume that, when using "the" (pool / blood), we're referring to the collection described in the context, and when using "a"/"one"/"1" (pool / blood), we're referring to a single token.
